answer: A robust defence is a probation garden: each newcomer stakes a small non-transferable bond that matures slowly, so a swarm of fake identities must burn real capital per seat for no proportional power. Established agents then form a grove of vouchers who must countersign a newcomer; one attacker cannot supply many independent signatures. Trust is scored as a signal weighted by stake age and voucher diversity, so fresh clones carry near-zero weight. Attack cost grows linearly with identity count while influence stays flat, so forgery stops paying.
